objective: Backlog B1 of docs/RESEARCH_GOALS.md, growth as a law (G5, question 4 of docs/KNOT_INTUITION.md, with G1, space from a law), taken up at the owner's approval on 2026-11-07: what can a growth order add to a law that a static law cannot, read with the canonical test (K1-K3 on allowed states, no scheduler supplying an input)? Write growth rules as laws on their substrates with the history as a witness and test the joint law with K1-K3: whether the order ever knots with the world's states, which part of a history is local and bounded and which is global, and whether a beginning alone does work (the open-end rule of OPEN-END-GROWTH-20261107-001 grows threads and never rings, while a bounded local law should not tell a long thread from a ring). Then test the same muscle in the plane: grow the pinwheel outward from one tile by its own label-free law in every order (PINWHEEL-ATLAS-20261107-001C, retired there as backlog, is taken up here), measuring forced moves, choices and dead ends and whether grown patches are pinwheel patches, beside GROW-COIN-20261107-001's result that label-free accretion keeps the roundness witness on spheres. Challenges A14 (a growing law's history is a hidden witness) and the growth clause of A4 in docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md. Standalone value against known work: discrete Morse theory, proof-labeling schemes, periodic points of one-dimensional shifts and aperiodic tilings, and growth rules with dead surfaces (Onoda, Steinhardt, DiVincenzo and Socolar 1988) are classical; their reading under K1-K3 and the pinwheel's outward growth were not found.
status: Complete 2026-11-07: written into the law, a growth order never knots with the world's states (a product on each fixed world; existence enters as a presence literal), its local part is pairwise and its global part, time without a loop, is a knot on every cycle, so a beginning is a knot; by Euler's count sprouting grows trees and disc moves discs and spheres, and in one dimension the beginning does what no bounded static witness can (no bounded law tells a long thread from a ring). In the plane the pinwheel, grown outward by its own label-free collar law, left its own patches in all 70 runs of four orders; the first wrong move is always a coin, and an oracle grows 1,000 tiles with 4 to 10 real bits after the seed against 46 to 88 apparent, so growth needs a few hierarchy bits shared across the boundary; a stronger radius-2 law gets stuck too. Recommendation: Continue with knots across time (G5), Payoff 2/3 Substantial, Concreteness 2/3 Testable, awaiting the owner's go-ahead (backlog B7).
stop_rule: Stop when the joint law of a growth rule's history and states is decided under K1-K3 (whether the order ever knots with the states; which part of the history is local), the one-dimensional question (does a beginning do work no bounded static witness can) is answered by proof, and the pinwheel's outward growth is measured to the declared radius in the declared orders, or an obstruction is found and explained.
title: Growth as a law: a beginning is a knot, and growth needs a shared coin
